Dear Rep. Jacobs,

How absolutely mesmerizing to witness your latest contribution to the theater of statistical horror! "Kick 16 million people off their health care" and "put 300 rural hospitals on the brink of closure" – such remarkably precise catastrophic predictions from someone who apparently has a direct line to some kind of legislative crystal ball. Your talent for manufacturing specific casualty counts without citing actual bill text is truly impressive.

Since you mentioned Senate Republicans passing Trump's "horrific budget" but I haven't seen the Senate version because it hasn't been uploaded yet, I'll address your doomsday prophecy based on HR1 since reconciliation will be required anyway.

But first, let's examine your fascinating political strategy contradiction: you call this budget "horrific" and claim it will devastate healthcare, close hospitals, and starve children. Here's a revolutionary thought, Sara – if Republicans just passed legislation that will supposedly kick 16 million people off healthcare and close 300 rural hospitals, wouldn't brilliant politics be to let them own this disaster and ride the voter outrage to massive Democratic victories? Your desperate "NO" vote reveals what you actually know: this bill helps working families, which is precisely why you're frantically trying to block benefits that would improve their lives. For someone representing San Diego, this seems like remarkably poor political instincts.

I'm also confused by your underlying premise about tax policy, Representative. The left's narrative for years has been that the wealthy don't pay taxes – remember all those viral posts about billionaires paying less than their secretaries and corporations paying zero federal taxes? Yet you're simultaneously opposing tax breaks for the rich. How exactly can you get a tax break when you don't pay taxes? This seems like a fundamental logical contradiction in your messaging strategy. Either the wealthy pay substantial taxes (and thus can receive breaks) or they don't pay taxes (making breaks impossible). Which narrative are we using today?

Let's examine your apocalyptic fiction:

"Kick 16 million people off their health care" – This appears nowhere in HR1's 1,000+ pages. The bill implements work requirements for able-bodied adults through Section 44141 (Page 818, Line 1) with broad exemptions for pregnant women, veterans, foster youth, caregivers, homeless, and disabled individuals. It maintains all coverage for children, seniors, and disabled individuals, and continues CHIP funding. Please cite which section of the Senate bill removes 16 million people from coverage.

"Put 300 rural hospitals on the brink of closure" – Remarkably specific! Which section mandates endangering exactly 300 rural hospitals? Did they include a hospital vulnerability index with specific facility names?

"Close 200 Planned Parenthoods" – Another precise prediction! Please cite the section requiring closure of exactly 200 Planned Parenthood facilities. This provision doesn't exist in HR1.

"Make millions more kids hungry" – SNAP reforms under Sections 10002 & 10008 (Pages 18, 25) maintain all exemptions for families with children while focusing work requirements on able-bodied adults 18-65. Children remain fully protected. How does ensuring able-bodied adults work, study, or volunteer make children hungry?

Since none of these specific catastrophic provisions appear in HR1, are you voting against bills based on horror movie scripts you're writing for political theater?

Meanwhile, here's what you're actually voting to deny San Diego families:

Tax Relief You're Blocking for Working Californians:
Permanent Trump-era tax cuts including lower brackets and doubled standard deduction (Sections 110001–110004, Pages 961–962)
Exempting tips from taxation – helping restaurant workers, hotel staff, hairdressers across San Diego (Section 110101, Page 972)
Exempting overtime pay from taxes – rewarding hard work (Section 110102, Page 972)
Enhanced standard deduction for seniors (Section 110103)
Car loan interest deduction (Section 110104)
Modified SALT deduction cap to $30,000 – particularly helpful for California families (Section 112018, Page 982)

Healthcare EXPANSION You're Opposing:
Enhanced Health Savings Accounts with higher contribution limits (Sections 110201–110213, Pages 976–980)
HSA eligibility extended to Medicare Part A recipients
HSA spending allowed for fitness and wellness programs
Expanded healthcare savings options for San Diego families

Economic Benefits You're Fighting Against:
Increased safety net for California farmers: wheat prices up to $6.35, corn to $4.10, soybeans to $10.00 (Section 10101, Pages 28–30)
Enhanced support for beginning farmers
National security investment creating jobs in San Diego's defense sector (Title II, Pages 4–5)
Rural infrastructure and school program extensions

Accountability Measures You Consider "Horrific":
Work requirements for able-bodied adults with extensive exemptions (Section 44141, Page 818)
Citizenship verification for program eligibility (Section 44110, Page 804)
Ending federal subsidies for administrative waste (Section 10007, Page 24)
State cost-sharing for SNAP benefits to ensure program integrity (Section 10006, Page 22)

So let me understand your position, Representative: enhanced healthcare savings somehow kicks people off healthcare, tax relief for tip workers endangers rural hospitals, permanent middle-class tax cuts close Planned Parenthoods, and ensuring able-bodied adults contribute to society starves children?

You either didn't read the bill and are just manufacturing statistical horrors for political theater, aren't smart enough to understand that your specific predictions need to actually appear in legislative text, or are fine deceiving San Diego families about legislation that would enhance their healthcare options and put money in their pockets. Which is it, Representative?

Perhaps between your statistical fiction and your dramatic "NO" vote, you could explain to working families in San Diego why they don't deserve tax relief on tips and overtime, enhanced healthcare savings, and expanded economic opportunities while you fight to preserve government waste and fraud.

Your constituents deserve better than apocalyptic fan fiction masquerading as legislative analysis. If this bill truly creates the disaster you describe with such mathematical precision, shouldn't you be thanking Republicans for supposedly handing Democrats the easiest campaign issues in history?
